decisions.question: S30's gates nidana.runtime.5 to .11 assume the replay tool passes bus_activation_test.dart (bus-api@v1's binding of topology-dsl@v1's live suite) when no case of it falls within --guarantee. Does that agree with nidana.model D2, or is it a request-style assumption conflicting with another node's entry (a collision)?

options.label: agree
options.consequence: No collision. D2 item 4 (a slug's behavior cases run only as the restriction admits them; a slug with no id in the restriction runs none of them) and ADR-001 item 9 (a bare G{n} is the replayed slug's; the tool learns a binding's suite from the conformance library it imports; a case runs only when every id it covers is in the restriction) leave the live binding with no admitted case at .5 to .11, and D2 item 1 fails a run only on a failing or PENDING fixture. The two implementation hazards the experiment shows go to the hsdd-adr clarification of ADR-001 item 9 already recommended at S29.

options.label: disagree
options.consequence: A collision: stop before applying anything; the orchestrator would arbitrate between changing nidana.runtime's gates and changing nidana.model's tool semantics.

decisions.why: Both texts make an excluded case not run and neither makes an empty selection a failure or a usage error; nidana.model.6's scope adds 'a slug with no id in the restriction runs no binding'. Read with ADR-001 item 9, the slug that matters for a binding is the slug of the suite it imports (topology-dsl), which has no id at .5 to .11. The experiment found two ways a tool could still fail the gates, neither of which D2 permits: dart test exits 79 ('No tests ran') when the name filter admits nothing (E2), and nidana.runtime.11's bare bus-api ids used as a raw name filter would run topology-dsl's same-numbered live cases G18 to G21, G24 and G29 before the pipeline is wired (E3). The per-binding empty case is implied rather than stated, hence medium confidence. The signal that would have changed my mind: D2 or nidana.model.6 stating that a binding whose filter admits no case is run anyway, or is an error.
evidence: hsdd/spec/nidana.model.md D2 items 1 and 4, nidana.model.6 Scope

decisions.question: The G41 amend makes getCurrentValue and getBufferedValues throw TypeError at the call for an off-type value, while G8 says 'neither throws except TopicCollision'. Is the amend still compatible, and what happens to G8?

options.label: compatible; G8 names the TypeError
options.consequence: G41 gains the off-type clause and G8 reads 'neither throws except TopicCollision, or the TypeError G41 states for a value that is not of the topic's value type'; v1 kept with a Versioning line.

options.label: breaking; stop for the owner
options.consequence: The run stops until the orchestrator decides whether to bump bus-api to v2 or drop the amend.

options.label: apply G41 only
options.consequence: The contract reads as self-contradictory between G8 and G41.

decisions.why: Before the amend no behavior conformed to G8 for an off-type current value: G8 also says getCurrentValue is the last value delivered, which is not of the type the call returns, and topic-model@v1 offers generic code no way to check a value against a topic's type at publish (nidana.runtime D4, D5), so an implementation could only throw or return a value G8 does not allow. No consumer can have relied on a no-throw result. flutter-binding@v1 G5 builds from getCurrentValue but states nothing for an off-type value, and no fixture of any contract publishes one. A careful engineer might still have shown the owner the G8 edit, since it touches a throw statement the Breaking list names. The signal that would have changed my mind: a consumer contract or fixture expecting a fallback value for an off-type current value.

decisions.question: The amend entry says each conversion runs 'in the delivery callback of the one subscription or topology read it serves' and lists the conversions made at a call. A read's connection is converted during activate. Does the G41 text say which rule covers it?

options.label: state the connection explicitly
options.consequence: G41 says 'its first values and a read's connection included'; an off-type connection value goes to the provider zone's handler and activate returns normally; case three pins it.

options.label: keep the entry's wording
options.consequence: A reader could take the connection for a conversion made during activate and expect activate to throw, which nidana.runtime.12's scope does not do.

decisions.why: D4 has every topology read convert each payload and nidana.runtime.12's scope converts 'each value' in the read's own callback, connection values included; only the reduceInto seed throws to the caller. Saying so removes the one ambiguity a consumer could build on. The signal that would have changed my mind: a plan text that throws from activate for an off-type connection value.
